defects.problem: The orchestra is called brass-free, although the score and the page’s own timeline contain four horns.
defects.fix: Replace ‘brass-free, chamber-like orchestra’ with ‘chamber-like orchestra without trumpets, trombones or percussion’ or simply ‘chamber-like orchestra’.

defects.problem: The near-doubling of detected onset density is called a doubling of pulse density. The report counts detected attacks, not beats or musical pulse.
defects.fix: Replace ‘the pulse doubles in density’ with ‘the report detects roughly twice as many attacks’ or a score-grounded statement about the more active texture, without asserting a doubled beat.

defects.problem: The omission of the weaving woman is supported, but Gautier’s French first-person speaker is not identified as a man in the cited text. The claim that Gautier specifically made a lonely man is stronger than the evidence.
defects.evidence: http://www.mahlerarchives.net/Archive%20documents/DLvDE/Der_Einsame.htm — Le soir d’automne uses an ungendered first-person speaker and removes the weaving scene.
defects.fix: Replace ‘a lonely man’s autumn evening’ with ‘a lonely speaker’s autumn evening’.

defects.problem: The late harp writing is called glissandi. These score passages are fully notated, chordal arpeggiated runs in sextuplets, unlike the score’s explicitly marked glissandi elsewhere.
defects.evidence: https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/6/65/IMSLP20582-PMLP47886-Mahler_-_Das_Lied_von_der_Erde_(orch._score).pdf — printed pp.47–49, both harps in unison, with the individual pitches and tuplets written out.
defects.fix: Replace ‘harp glissandi’ with ‘harp arpeggios’ in both places. The broader description of sweeping unison harps can remain.
